claim: In the AWS guide, a Site-to-Site VPN connection is the connection between your VPC and your own on-premises network, and the service supports IPsec VPN connections.
q: What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN in one sentence?
v: connection between your VPC and your own on-premises network
a connection between your VPC and your own on-premises network
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN

Although the term VPN connection is a general term, in this documentation, a VPN connection refers to the connection between your VPC and your own on-premises network. Site-to-Site VPN supports Internet Protocol security (IPsec) VPN connections.

claim: A VPN tunnel is an encrypted link where data can pass from the customer network to or from AWS.
q: What is a VPN tunnel in Site-to-Site VPN?
v: An encrypted link where data can pass from the customer network to or from AWS
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN
VPN tunnel: An encrypted link where data can pass from the customer network to or from AWS.

claim: A customer gateway is an AWS resource that gives AWS information about your customer gateway device. The customer gateway device is the physical device or software application on your side of the connection.
q: What is the difference between a customer gateway and a customer gateway device?
v: An AWS resource which provides information to AWS about your customer gateway device
A physical device or software application on your side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN
Customer gateway: An AWS resource which provides information to AWS about your customer gateway device.
docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN
Customer gateway device: A physical device or software application on your side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection.

claim: Creating the customer gateway resource in AWS does not configure or create the customer gateway device. You must configure the device yourself.
q: Does creating a customer gateway resource in AWS configure the on-premises device?
v: does not configure or create the customer gateway device
You must configure the device yourself
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/your-cgw
The customer gateway resource in AWS does not configure or create the customer gateway device. You must configure the device yourself.

claim: Target gateway is a generic term for the VPN endpoint on the Amazon side of the connection; it can be a virtual private gateway or a transit gateway.
q: What does target gateway mean for a Site-to-Site VPN connection?
v: A generic term for the VPN endpoint on the Amazon side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection
as a VPN endpoint for the Amazon side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN
Target gateway: A generic term for the VPN endpoint on the Amazon side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection.
docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN
Transit gateway: A transit hub that can be used to interconnect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks, and as a VPN endpoint for the Amazon side of the Site-to-Site VPN connection.

claim: A virtual private gateway can be attached to one VPC at a time. To connect the same VPN connection to several VPCs, AWS recommends exploring a transit gateway.
q: How many VPCs can one virtual private gateway be attached to, and what does AWS recommend for several VPCs?
v: attach one virtual private gateway to a VPC at a time
explore using a transit gateway instead
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits
You can attach one virtual private gateway to a VPC at a time. To connect the same Site-to-Site VPN connection to multiple VPCs, we recommend that you explore using a transit gateway instead.

claim: Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway are subject to the total transit gateway attachments limit.
q: Do VPN connections on a transit gateway count against the transit gateway attachment quota?
v: subject to the total transit gateway attachments limit
Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits
Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway are subject to the total transit gateway attachments limit.

claim: Each Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels, each with a unique public IP address. AWS says to configure both tunnels for redundancy; when one is unavailable, traffic is routed automatically to the other.
q: How many tunnels does a Site-to-Site VPN connection have, and why configure both?
v: has two tunnels, with each tunnel using a unique public IP address
two tunnels, each with its own public IP address
network traffic is automatically routed to the available tunnel
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPNTunnels

Each Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels, with each tunnel using a unique public IP address. It is important to configure both tunnels for redundancy. When one tunnel becomes unavailable (for example, down for maintenance), network traffic is automatically routed to the available tunnel for that specific Site-to-Site VPN connection.

claim: The two tunnels of a Site-to-Site VPN connection end in different Availability Zones. If a device fails inside AWS, the connection fails over to the second tunnel so access is not interrupted.
q: In which Availability Zones do the two tunnels of a Site-to-Site VPN connection terminate, and what happens on an AWS device failure?
v: each terminating in a different Availability Zone
each tunnel ends in a different Availability Zone
automatically fails over to the second tunnel
it fails over to the second tunnel on its own
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/disaster-recovery-resiliency

A Site-to-Site VPN connection consists of two tunnels, each terminating in a different Availability Zone, to provide increased availability to your VPC. If there's a device failure within AWS, your VPN connection automatically fails over to the second tunnel so that your access isn't interrupted.

claim: AWS applies tunnel endpoint updates to one tunnel of a VPN connection at a time. During an update the connection might briefly lose redundancy, so both tunnels should be configured for high availability.
q: What can happen to a Site-to-Site VPN connection when AWS updates a tunnel endpoint?
v: AWS applies tunnel endpoint updates to one tunnel of your VPN connection at a time
AWS updates one tunnel at a time
might experience a brief loss of redundancy
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/endpoint-replacements

AWS applies tunnel endpoint updates to one tunnel of your VPN connection at a time. During a tunnel endpoint update, your VPN connection might experience a brief loss of redundancy. It’s therefore important to configure both tunnels in your VPN connection for high availability.

claim: During a tunnel endpoint replacement, connectivity over the tunnel might be interrupted while the new tunnel endpoint is provisioned. Replacement happens when AWS performs tunnel updates or when you modify your VPN connection.
q: When is a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel endpoint replaced, and what is the effect?
v: connectivity over the tunnel might be interrupted
when AWS performs tunnel updates, or when you modify your VPN connection
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/endpoint-replacements

Sometimes, one or both of the VPN tunnel endpoints is replaced when AWS performs tunnel updates, or when you modify your VPN connection. During a tunnel endpoint replacement, connectivity over the tunnel might be interrupted while the new tunnel endpoint is provisioned.

claim: Traffic in each tunnel can be encrypted with AES128 or AES256 and uses Diffie-Hellman groups for key exchange, which provides Perfect Forward Secrecy. AWS authenticates with SHA1 or SHA2 hashing functions.
q: Which encryption and hashing functions protect traffic in a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel?
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/data-protection

Each Site-to-Site VPN connection consists of two encrypted IPsec VPN tunnels that link AWS and your network. Traffic in each tunnel can be encrypted with AES128 or AES256 and use Diffie-Hellman groups for key exchange, providing Perfect Forward Secrecy. AWS authenticates with SHA1 or SHA2 hashing functions.

claim: The customer gateway device can use IKEv1 or IKEv2 for the IKE security association. With IKEv1, only Main mode is supported.
q: Which IKE versions does Site-to-Site VPN support?
v: We support Main mode only with IKEv1
scope: IKE security association of a tunnel
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/CGRequirements
The following versions are supported: IKEv1 and IKEv2. We support Main mode only with IKEv1.

claim: A standard VPN connection crosses multiple public networks on the internet before it reaches the AWS VPN endpoint, which can give inconsistent availability and performance.
q: Does Site-to-Site VPN traffic travel over the public internet, and what is the drawback?
v: traffic traverses through multiple public networks on the internet
traffic crosses many public networks on the internet
scope: VPN connections that are not accelerated
ev: www/vpn/faqs
VPN connections face inconsistent availability and performance as traffic traverses through multiple public networks on the internet before reaching the VPN endpoint in AWS.

claim: A pre-shared key is the default authentication option for Site-to-Site VPN tunnels. You can specify your own key or let AWS generate one.
q: What is the default authentication option for Site-to-Site VPN tunnels?
v: A pre-shared key (PSK) is the default authentication option
a pre-shared key is the default
allow AWS to auto-generate one for you
cond: you can choose a certificate instead
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-tunnel-authentication-options
A pre-shared key (PSK) is the default authentication option for Site-to-Site VPN tunnels. When creating a tunnel, you can either specify your own PSK or allow AWS to auto-generate one for you.

claim: Instead of pre-shared keys, you can use a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority to authenticate the VPN.
q: How can Site-to-Site VPN tunnels be authenticated without pre-shared keys?
v: a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority
If you do not want to use pre-shared keys
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-tunnel-authentication-options
If you do not want to use pre-shared keys, you can use a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority to authenticate your VPN.

claim: You can store pre-shared keys in AWS Secrets Manager rather than directly in the Site-to-Site VPN service.
q: Where can a Site-to-Site VPN pre-shared key be stored besides the VPN service itself?
v: store pre-shared keys (PSKs) in AWS Secrets Manager
store the pre-shared key in AWS Secrets Manager
rather than directly in the Site-to-Site VPN service
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/enhanced-security

A key improvement is the ability to store pre-shared keys (PSKs) in AWS Secrets Manager rather than directly in the Site-to-Site VPN service, allowing for better secret management and compliance with security best practices.

claim: By default, your customer gateway device must bring up the tunnels by generating traffic and starting the IKE negotiation. You can configure the tunnels so that AWS initiates or restarts the negotiation instead.
q: Which side starts the IKE negotiation by default, and can AWS start it instead?
v: your customer gateway device must bring up the tunnels
the customer gateway device brings up the tunnels by default
AWS must initiate or restart the IKE negotiation process instead
you can make AWS start the negotiation
cond: set the startup action to make AWS initiate
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels

By default, your customer gateway device must bring up the tunnels for your Site-to-Site VPN connection by generating traffic and initiating the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) negotiation process. You can configure your VPN tunnels to specify that AWS must initiate or restart the IKE negotiation process instead.

claim: By default, when dead peer detection times out, the IKE session is stopped, the tunnel goes down and the routes are removed. You can set AWS to restart the IKE session, or to take no action.
q: What is the default DPD timeout action of a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel?
v: the IKE session is stopped, the tunnel goes down, and the routes are removed
the tunnel goes down and the routes are removed
AWS must restart the IKE session when DPD timeout occurs, or you can specify that AWS must take no action
scope: DPD timeout action of a tunnel
cond: after dead peer detection (DPD) timeout occurs
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels

DPD timeout action: The action to take after dead peer detection (DPD) timeout occurs. By default, the IKE session is stopped, the tunnel goes down, and the routes are removed. You can specify that AWS must restart the IKE session when DPD timeout occurs, or you can specify that AWS must take no action when DPD timeout occurs.

claim: For AWS to initiate IKE negotiation, AWS requires the public IP address of your customer gateway device, and IKE initiation from the AWS side is supported for IKEv2 only.
q: What are the requirements for letting AWS initiate the IKE negotiation of a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel?
v: AWS requires the public IP address of your customer gateway device
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels

To initiate IKE negotiation, AWS requires the public IP address of your customer gateway device. If you configured certificate-based authentication for your VPN connection and you did not specify an IP address when you created the customer gateway resource in AWS, you must create a new customer gateway and specify the IP address.
docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels
IKE initiation (startup action) from the AWS side of the VPN connection is supported for IKEv2 only.

claim: If the customer gateway device is behind a NAT device, you use the IP address of the NAT device as the customer gateway address, and UDP port 500 (and 4500 when NAT traversal is used) must be allowed.
q: What IP address do you give AWS when the customer gateway device is behind a NAT device, and which UDP ports must be open?
v: use the IP address of your NAT device
use the IP address of the NAT device
UDP packets on port 500 (and port 4500, if NAT traversal is being used)
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/cgw-options

For IPv4 addresses: If your customer gateway device is behind a network address translation (NAT) device, use the IP address of your NAT device. Also, ensure that UDP packets on port 500 (and port 4500, if NAT traversal is being used) are allowed to pass between your network and the AWS Site-to-Site VPN endpoints.

claim: The IP address of the customer gateway device's external interface must be static, and can be IPv4 or IPv6. It is not required when you use a private certificate from AWS Private CA with a public VPN.
q: What kind of IP address does the customer gateway device need?
v: The IP address must be static
An IP address is not required when you are using a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority and a public VPN
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/cgw-options
The IP address must be static and can be either IPv4 or IPv6.
docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/cgw-options
An IP address is not required when you are using a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority and a public VPN.

claim: Site-to-Site VPN is a route-based solution. If the customer gateway device uses a policy-based configuration, you must limit it to a single security association.
q: Does Site-to-Site VPN support policy-based VPN devices?
v: The Site-to-Site VPN service is a route-based solution
you must limit your configuration to a single security association (SA)
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/CGRequirements
The Site-to-Site VPN service is a route-based solution. If you are using a policy-based configuration, you must limit your configuration to a single security association (SA).

claim: For dynamically routed VPN connections, the customer gateway device uses BGP to exchange routes with the virtual private gateway. All BGP traffic is encrypted and sent through the IPsec security association.
q: What does the customer gateway device need for dynamic routing, and is the BGP traffic encrypted?
v: BGP is used to exchange routes between the customer gateway device and the virtual private gateway
All BGP traffic is encrypted and transmitted via the IPsec Security Association
ev: docs/vpn/latest/s2svpn/CGRequirements

BGP is used to exchange routes between the customer gateway device and the virtual private gateway for devices that use BGP. All BGP traffic is encrypted and transmitted via the IPsec Security Association.
